results.title: Where have Ghana’s fireflies and antlions gone?
results.content: For many Ghanaians, childhood memories of the outdoors include tiny lights flickering through the darkness as fireflies moved across the night, and small, funnel-shaped pits in sandy ground where antlions, locally known as kokroko, lay in wait for their prey. These encounters were once familiar sights for some people. Today, however, some Ghanaians say they rarely see these insects, raising questions about whether their populations are declining and what might explain their apparent disappearance. While these observations do not, on their own, establish a nationwide decline, they point to a question worth investigating: what has happened to the insects that once formed part of everyday life in many communities?

results.title: Ghana Publishing Company launches online bookshop for Acts of Parliament, Constitution
results.content: Ghanaians can now order Acts of Parliament, copies of the Constitution and other official publications online and have them delivered to their locations without travelling to Accra. The service follows the introduction of an online bookshop by the Ghana Publishing Company Limited (GPCL) to improve public access to government publications. Speaking at a press conference in Accra on Monday, October 19, 2026, GPCL Managing Director, Nana Kwasi Boatey, Esq., said the initiative was designed to address the difficulties people face in obtaining copies of Ghana’s laws. He explained that people living outside Accra often had to travel long distances to purchase Acts of Parliament and other publications, sometimes spending more on transportation than on the documents themselves.
